title: Connected to Wi-Fi but No Internet Access
symptoms: Wi-Fi icon shows connected
Yellow exclamation mark or 'No Internet, Secured'
Websites fail to open with DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NO_INTERNET
Network ping to external IPs times out
possibleCauses: Router or ISP gateway outage
Corrupted local DNS cache or invalid DNS server assignment
Stale DHCP IP lease or IP address conflict
Third-party VPN or antivirus network filtering hook blocking traffic
initialQuestion: Can another device (such as your phone or another laptop) connected to the SAME Wi-Fi network access websites?

start.instruction: Test internet connectivity on a second device connected to the identical Wi-Fi network.
start.question: Can another device connected to the same Wi-Fi access the internet?

options.label: YES
options.summary: Other devices work, confirming the issue is localized to this computer.

options.label: NO
options.summary: No devices have internet, pointing to a router, modem, or ISP outage.

router-reboot-isp.instruction: Power-cycle your Wi-Fi router and modem: Unplug the power cable from both devices, wait 30 full seconds, reconnect the modem first until solid green lights show, then reconnect the router.
router-reboot-isp.question: Did power cycling the router and modem restore internet access?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Router power cycle successfully cleared stalled routing tables and refreshed external ISP handshake.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Router reboot did not restore connectivity.

check-modem-wan.instruction: Check the WAN / Internet LED indicator on your modem or fiber ONT. Is the Internet light red, orange, blinking rapidly, or completely off?
check-modem-wan.question: Is the modem's Internet light red/unlit, indicating an ISP service interruption?

options.label: YES
options.escalationReason: Physical WAN signal loss detected at the modem level. ISP line technician or service provider dispatch required.

options.label: NO
options.summary: WAN indicator looks normal, but traffic is not routing.

router-factory-or-support.instruction: Check if your ISP account has an active billing lock or localized area maintenance outage via your mobile data app.
router-factory-or-support.question: Did your ISP report an active service outage or maintenance in your area?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Issue confirmed as scheduled ISP maintenance in your sector. Service will resume automatically upon ISP completion.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Unresolved router hardware or gateway firmware failure. Network engineering support requested.

check-dns-local.instruction:
Flush your local DNS resolver and reset TCP/IP stack. Open Command Prompt (or Terminal) as Administrator and execute:
1) ipconfig /flushdns
2) netsh winsock reset
3) Restart your laptop.
check-dns-local.question: After restarting your laptop, can you now load web pages?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Flushing stale DNS cache and resetting Winsock catalog resolved the network routing glitch.

options.label: NO
options.summary: DNS cache flush did not resolve; testing DNS server configuration.

check-custom-dns.instruction: Manually configure reliable public DNS servers. Go to Network Adapter Settings > IPv4 Properties > Set Preferred DNS to 8.8.8.8 (Google) and Alternate DNS to 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare).
check-custom-dns.question: Did changing your DNS server to 8.8.8.8 allow websites to open?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Default ISP DNS server was failing or timing out. Switched to high-availability public DNS.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Public DNS did not resolve; checking for proxy or VPN interception.

check-vpn-proxy.instruction: Temporarily disable any active VPN software, proxy servers, or third-party web filtering suites (e.g. NordVPN, Zscaler, Cloudflare WARP).
check-vpn-proxy.question: Does disabling VPN/proxy restore immediate internet access?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: A disconnected or misconfigured VPN kill-switch was blocking all outbound traffic.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Local network adapter driver corruption or persistent routing table failure requires Tier 2 IT support escalation.

title: Laptop Overheating & Fan Noise
symptoms: Laptop chassis feels extremely hot to touch
Cooling fans spinning constantly at maximum RPM
Sudden thermal shutdowns or freezes during normal tasks
CPU thermal throttling causing severe system lag
possibleCauses: Air intake vents or exhaust grills clogged with dust and lint
Laptop operated on soft surfaces (bed, couch, blanket) blocking airflow
High CPU/GPU utilization caused by background runaway processes or crypto malware
Degraded or dried thermal paste between CPU heat sink and die
initialQuestion: Is the laptop currently placed directly on a soft surface like a bed, blanket, or your lap, or is it on a hard, flat desk?

start.instruction: Inspect laptop placement and airflow intake clearance.
start.question: Is the laptop currently placed on a soft surface (bed/blanket/cushion) or on a hard flat desk?

options.label: SOFT SURFACE
options.summary: Laptop is on fabric or soft surface which traps heat and suffocates intake vents.

options.label: HARD DESK
options.summary: Placement is adequate; investigating thermal dust obstruction and processor load.

move-to-hard-surface.instruction: Move the laptop immediately to a clean, elevated hard flat surface. Elevate the rear feet with a book or stand by 1 inch to allow ambient air intake. Wait 10 minutes.
move-to-hard-surface.question: Did moving to a hard surface and elevating the rear lower the fan noise and temperatures?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Intake airflow was restored. Operating laptops on soft bedding severely suffocates cooling vents.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Chassis remains hot even on desk; checking computational load.

check-task-manager-cpu.instruction: Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc or Activity Monitor on Mac). Sort processes by CPU usage. Is any unknown process consuming more than 40% CPU continuously?
check-task-manager-cpu.question: Is there a runaway process consuming unusually high CPU?

options.label: YES
options.summary: Identified high-utilization background process generating heat.

options.label: NO
options.summary: CPU utilization is low/normal, meaning the thermal dissipation system is physically failing.

terminate-runaway-process.instruction: Select the heavy background process and click 'End Task'. If it is an unwanted software or browser tab, close or uninstall it.
terminate-runaway-process.question: Did terminating that process cause temperatures and fan noise to decrease?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Rogue high-utilization background process terminated, restoring thermal equilibrium.

options.label: NO
options.summary: System remains hot even with process terminated.

check-physical-dust.instruction: Power off the laptop and inspect the exhaust vents with a flashlight. Use a can of compressed air with short bursts to clear dust build-up from the fin stack.
check-physical-dust.question: Did clearing dust from the ventilation ports solve the overheating issue?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Dust clumps in heat sink fins cleared, allowing unrestricted thermal exhaust.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Persistent overheating despite low CPU load and clear vents points to dried thermal paste or failed bearing cooling fan. Hardware technician required.

title: Slow Laptop Performance & System Freezing
symptoms: Applications take a very long time to open
Spinning circle/wheel cursor frequently appears
Typing or mouse movements lag
High RAM or 100% Disk usage in Task Manager
possibleCauses: Too many startup applications launching automatically
Low available RAM causing heavy virtual memory disk swapping
Mechanical HDD operating at 100% active time
Corrupted Windows search indexer or temporary cache bloat
initialQuestion: Does the laptop run slowly immediately upon booting up, or only after you open multiple applications?

start.instruction: Assess whether the bottleneck is boot/startup background bloat or resource exhaustion during multitasking.
start.question: Does the slowdown occur immediately at startup or only after launching several programs?

options.label: RIGHT FROM BOOT
options.summary: Slowness at startup indicates startup bloat or background services.

options.label: AFTER OPENING APPS
options.summary: Slowness during multitasking indicates RAM or VRAM exhaustion.

check-startup-apps.instruction: Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc > Navigate to the 'Startup Apps' tab. Disable heavy third-party startup items (Discord, Spotify, Steam, Updaters). Restart your computer.
check-startup-apps.question: Did disabling non-essential startup apps improve boot time and responsiveness?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Disabled unnecessary background startup hooks, freeing CPU and disk I/O at launch.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Startup items disabled, but system remains sluggish.

check-disk-usage-100.instruction: Open Task Manager > Performance tab > Click 'Disk'. Is the Active Time pegged at or near 100% even when idle?
check-disk-usage-100.question: Is Disk Active Time stuck at 100%?

options.label: YES
options.summary: Identified 100% Disk Active Time bottleneck.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Disk utilization normal; cleaning temp files and verifying integrity.

disable-sysmain.instruction: Disable the SysMain (Superfetch) service: Press Win + R, type 'services.msc', find 'SysMain', right-click > Stop, and set Startup type to Disabled.
disable-sysmain.question: Did stopping SysMain drop the disk usage and speed up the system?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: SysMain aggressive prefetching was saturating disk read queues. Service disabled successfully.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Persistent 100% disk usage often indicates imminent storage drive failure (bad sectors) or need for SSD upgrade.

check-ram-capacity.instruction: Check RAM usage in Task Manager. If Memory is exceeding 85%, close unused browser tabs (especially media tabs) and background helper tools.
check-ram-capacity.question: Did closing excess browser tabs reduce memory pressure and restore responsiveness?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: System was swapping active memory pages to disk pagefile due to high RAM utilization. Closing background tabs restored memory.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Memory is within bounds; scanning file system.

run-disk-cleanup.instruction: Run Windows Disk Cleanup (or clean temp files) and run 'sfc /scannow' in an Administrator Command Prompt to fix corrupt system binaries.
run-disk-cleanup.question: Did system file repair and temp file purge resolve the lag?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Corrupt Windows system files repaired and system cache cleared.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Hardware degradation or operating system profile corruption detected. IT support ticket required.

title: Web Browser Crashing or Closing Unexpectedly
symptoms: Browser closes abruptly without error message
'Aw, Snap!' or 'Out of Memory' crash screens
Browser freezes when playing video or scrolling heavy web pages
Tabs reload continuously
possibleCauses: Conflict with corrupted browser extensions (ad blockers, security extensions)
Corrupted browser profile, cache, or cookies database
Incompatible GPU hardware acceleration driver
Outdated browser build with unpatched memory leak
initialQuestion: Does the crash still happen if you open the browser in Incognito or Private Browsing mode?

start.instruction: Launch your browser in Incognito / Private window (Ctrl + Shift + N in Chrome/Edge, Ctrl + Shift + P in Firefox).
start.question: Does the browser work normally without crashing in Incognito / Private mode?

options.label: YES
options.summary: Incognito disables extensions, proving an extension is triggering the crash.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Crashing persists in Incognito, indicating core browser or GPU rendering conflict.

disable-extensions.instruction: Open your browser's Extension manager (e.g. chrome://extensions). Toggle off all extensions, then re-enable them one by one to isolate the culprit.
disable-extensions.question: Did disabling extensions stop the crashes?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Identified and eliminated incompatible or malicious browser extension causing crash.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Extensions were not the only cause; clearing cached data.

disable-hardware-acceleration.instruction: Go to Browser Settings > System > Disable 'Use graphics acceleration when available' (or Hardware Acceleration). Relaunch the browser.
disable-hardware-acceleration.question: Did turning off hardware acceleration prevent the crashes?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: GPU graphics driver conflict resolved by delegating web rendering to software mode.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Hardware acceleration was not the cause; proceeding to profile reset.

clear-browser-cache.instruction: Clear browsing data: Press Ctrl + Shift + Delete, select 'All time', check Cookies and Cached images and files, then click Clear Data.
clear-browser-cache.question: Did clearing cached web data resolve the issue?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Corrupt cached JavaScript or cookie database cleared.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Core browser binaries or profile database corrupted.

reinstall-browser.instruction: Export your bookmarks, uninstall the browser completely, download the latest official installer, and reinstall cleanly.
reinstall-browser.question: Did a clean browser reinstall solve the crashing?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Fresh installation replaced corrupted installation files.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: System-wide DLL conflict, RAM bit flip, or security software injection crash. Technical support review needed.

title: Printer Connected but Not Printing
symptoms: Printer status displays 'Offline' or 'Error - Printing'
Print jobs stuck indefinitely in print queue
Printer receives job but spits out blank page or blinking light
Network printer unreachable via IP address
possibleCauses: Windows Print Spooler service halted or jammed with corrupted spool file
Stale IP address assignment on wireless printer
Outdated or generic driver causing communication breakdown
Hardware paper feed sensor or ink cartridge communication fault
initialQuestion: Is the printer connected via USB cable directly to your computer, or wirelessly over your Wi-Fi network?

start.instruction: Determine the printer interface connection method.
start.question: Is the printer connected via Wi-Fi network or USB cable?

options.label: WI-FI / NETWORK
options.summary: Wireless printer connection path selected.

options.label: USB CABLE
options.summary: Direct USB hardware connection path selected.

check-printer-ip.instruction: Check the printer's screen or print a Network Configuration page. Verify the printer has an active IP address on your home subnet (e.g. 192.168.1.X).
check-printer-ip.question: Does the printer have a valid IP address and show connected to Wi-Fi?

options.label: YES
options.summary: Printer is on network; problem is with local queue or spooler.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Printer has dropped from the Wi-Fi network.

reconnect-printer-wifi.instruction: On the printer control panel, run the Wireless Setup Wizard to re-enter your Wi-Fi SSID and password. Ensure it connects to 2.4 GHz if required.
reconnect-printer-wifi.question: Did reconnecting the printer to Wi-Fi allow the test page to print?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Printer was reconnected to the wireless access point with valid DHCP lease.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Wireless connection restored but print jobs still not processing.

check-usb-port.instruction: Unplug the USB cable from both ends. Plug it into a different USB port directly on your computer (avoid unpowered USB hubs).
check-usb-port.question: Did reconnecting to a different USB port resolve the issue?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Faulty USB port or hub connection bypassed.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Hardware connection verified; checking Windows print spooler.

restart-print-spooler.instruction:
Reset the Print Spooler: Open Command Prompt as Admin and run:
1) net stop spooler
2) del /Q /F /S "%systemroot%\System32\Spool\Printers\*.*"
3) net start spooler
restart-print-spooler.question: Did clearing stuck print jobs and restarting the Print Spooler allow you to print?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Corrupted print queue cleared and Print Spooler daemon successfully restarted.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Printer driver corruption or hardware firmware failure requires manufacturer driver reinstallation or support dispatch.

title: Application Crashing or Won't Open
symptoms: Application crashes on launch with error dialog
Missing .dll file error (e.g. VCRUNTIME140.dll, MSVCP140.dll)
Program window flashes briefly then terminates
Application hung with 'Not Responding' status
possibleCauses: Missing or corrupted Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable runtime libraries
Corrupted application configuration file or registry keys
Security software quarantine or permissions limitation
Windows Compatibility mode mismatch
initialQuestion: Does the application show a specific error message (such as a missing DLL or error code) when it crashes?

start.instruction: Identify crash behavior and error messaging.
start.question: Does the app display a specific error code or DLL error, or does it close silently?

options.label: YES, ERROR SHOWN
options.summary: Explicit error code or DLL reported.

options.label: NO, JUST DISAPPEARS
options.summary: Silent crash indicating permission or execution policy failure.

check-vc-redist.instruction: If the error mentions a DLL like VCRUNTIME, MSVCP, or DirectX: Download and install the latest all-in-one Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x86 and x64) from official Microsoft support.
check-vc-redist.question: Did installing the Visual C++ Redistributables fix the launch error?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Missing shared C++ runtime dependencies installed.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Dependencies present; checking execution rights.

run-as-admin-compat.instruction: Right-click the application executable or shortcut > select 'Run as Administrator'. Alternatively, right-click > Properties > Compatibility > check 'Run this program in compatibility mode for Windows 10'.
run-as-admin-compat.question: Does running as administrator or in compatibility mode allow the app to run?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Elevated administrator privileges or legacy compatibility layer bypassed execution hurdle.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Application configuration files or binaries corrupted.

reinstall-app-clean.instruction: Perform a clean reinstall: Uninstall the software, delete its leftover folder in %AppData% and %LocalAppData%, then install the latest stable version.
reinstall-app-clean.question: Did a clean reinstallation resolve the application crash?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Corrupted application state and user profile settings cleared by fresh installation.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Unresolved software conflict or crash dump requires software engineering / IT application specialist.

title: Blue Screen (BSOD) or Boot Loop
symptoms: Blue Screen with Stop Code (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED, IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL, KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR)
System reboots into Automatic Repair loop
Stuck on manufacturer logo during boot
Windows failed update undoing changes
possibleCauses: Faulty device driver update (graphics, audio, or chipset)
Corrupted Windows BCD (Boot Configuration Data) or MBR
Failing memory module (RAM) or bad sectors on boot SSD
Recent incompatible Windows Cumulative Update
initialQuestion: Can the computer currently boot into Windows or Safe Mode, or is it stuck in a reboot loop before reaching the desktop?

start.question: Can you reach Windows desktop or Safe Mode, or does it crash before Windows loads?

options.label: CAN BOOT / SAFE MODE
options.summary: Desktop or Safe Mode accessible for diagnostics.

options.label: STUCK IN LOOP
options.summary: Pre-boot failure requiring Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE).

run-sfc-dism.instruction:
Run system file and component store repair. Open Command Prompt as Administrator:
1) DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-image /Restorehealth
2) sfc /scannow
Restart your computer when finished.
run-sfc-dism.question: Did DISM and SFC repair corrupted system files and stop the Blue Screens?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Corrupted kernel binaries and protected system components repaired via DISM and SFC.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Blue screen persists; checking recent driver or Windows updates.

rollback-driver-update.instruction: Roll back recent drivers or uninstall recent Windows Update: Go to Settings > Windows Update > Update History > Uninstall updates, or roll back your display driver in Device Manager.
rollback-driver-update.question: Did rolling back the recent update or driver restore system stability?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Problematic recent driver/update removed, restoring stable OS state.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Potential RAM hardware fault or catastrophic file system corruption. Critical hardware diagnostics required.

windows-recovery-env.instruction: In the Automatic Repair screen, select Advanced Options > Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > Startup Repair.
windows-recovery-env.question: Did Windows Startup Repair successfully diagnose and repair the boot loader?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Windows Startup Repair regenerated valid boot partition entries.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Startup repair could not fix boot loader.

system-restore-point.instruction: In Advanced Options, click 'System Restore' and select a restore point dated before the issue started.
system-restore-point.question: Did restoring to an earlier System Restore point restore normal booting?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: System configuration restored to previous known-good snapshot.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Unrecoverable boot corruption or failing storage controller. Tier 3 Enterprise support ticket required.

title: Low Disk Space or Drive Full Warnings
symptoms: 'Low Disk Space' notification warning on C: drive
Unable to install software or download files
System updates failing due to insufficient space
Red storage bar in File Explorer
possibleCauses: Accumulated Windows Update delivery optimization and temporary files
Uncleaned Recycle Bin and browser cache
Large hidden sleep/hibernation file (hiberfil.sys)
Unused bulky applications and games
initialQuestion: Do you need urgent space right away to install an update or file, or are you looking to clean up gigabytes permanently?

start.instruction: Initiate disk storage analysis and cleanup plan.
start.question: Do you want to run quick automatic cleanup or identify large hidden folders?

options.label: URGENT QUICK CLEANUP
options.summary: Quick automated purge of temp files and update leftovers.

options.label: COMPREHENSIVE AUDIT
options.summary: Full inspection of installed apps, large downloads, and hibernation file.

run-cleanmgr-admin.instruction: Press Win + R, type 'cleanmgr', select C: drive, click 'Clean up system files'. Check 'Previous Windows installation(s)', 'Temporary Windows installation files', and 'Recycle Bin'. Click OK.
run-cleanmgr-admin.question: Did running system file cleanup free up adequate space (several GBs)?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Purged obsolete OS installation cache, delivery optimization cache, and Recycle Bin.

options.label: NO
options.summary: Disk remains full; auditing large personal files and apps.

storage-sense-audit.instruction: Go to Windows Settings > System > Storage. Enable 'Storage Sense'. Click 'Installed apps' to sort by size and uninstall apps you no longer use.
storage-sense-audit.question: Did uninstalling large unused apps and enabling Storage Sense resolve the storage warning?

options.label: YES
options.resolutionText: Unused bulky applications uninstalled and automated Storage Sense cleaning enabled.

options.label: NO
options.escalationReason: Physical storage capacity is exhausted for user workload. SSD storage expansion or cloud archiving required.
